---
title: "01 - Generate MGtoolbox 3D probability: p28_330_HET_009"
author: "Xinyi Chen"
output: html_document
---

# Purpose

This file reads the raw three-dimensional image for the P28 sample,
detects somata using MGtoolbox, and applies spatial weights to image
intensities based on distance from the detected somata.

The resulting three-dimensional signal and soma information are saved
for subsequent analyses. A maximum-intensity projection is also exported
for visual inspection.

# Steps

1. Libraries
   Load MGtoolbox, which provides functions for image loading,
   soma detection, and spatial weighting.

2. Locate the project and define parameters
   Identify the project directory, specify the sample and file paths,
   and set the physical image dimensions, soma-detection parameters,
   and spatial-weighting parameters.

3. Read the 3D TIFF stack
   Read the raw TIFF stack into the three-dimensional array image_stack.

4. Construct the MGtoolbox stack object
   Store the image, physical dimensions, and output settings in a
   stackObj object. Create the required output directories and
   visualize the image.

5. Detect somas
   Detect somata and extract their centers and region information.
   Reuse the saved MDR calculation when available.

6. Generate the MGtoolbox 3D detected-signal stack
   Generate spatial weights from the detected soma positions and
   multiply them by the image intensities. Store the resulting
   three-dimensional signal as probability_3d.

7. Save the 3D results
   Save the weighted signal and stackObj as RDS files.
   Export soma centers and region information as CSV files.

8. Save a QC maximum-intensity projection
   Project the weighted signal along the axial direction and save
   a PNG for visual inspection. Subsequent three-dimensional analyses
   use the saved signal volume, rather than this projection.

9. Save the run summary
   Record the input file, image dimensions, parameter settings,
   number of detected somata, signal statistics, and output paths
   so that the processing can be traced.

The setup chunk controls R Markdown output formatting and is separate
from these processing steps.

```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  warning = FALSE,
  message = TRUE
)
```

## 1. Libraries

```{r libraries}
library(MGtoolbox)
```

## 2. Locate the project and define parameters

```{r paths-and-parameters}
find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
  current <- normalizePath(start, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)

  repeat {
    has_readme <- file.exists(file.path(current, "README.md"))
    has_notebooks <- dir.exists(file.path(current, "notebooks"))
    has_data <- dir.exists(file.path(current, "data"))

    if (has_readme && has_notebooks && has_data) {
      return(current)
    }

    parent <- dirname(current)
    if (identical(parent, current)) {
      stop("Open this file from within the repository containing README.md, notebooks/, and data/.")
    }
    current <- parent
  }
}

project_root <- find_project_root()

# Display and record paths relative to the repository root.
project_relative <- function(path) {
  prefix <- paste0(project_root, "/")

  if (!startsWith(path, prefix)) {
    stop("The path is outside the repository.")
  }

  substring(path, nchar(prefix) + 1L)
}

sample_name <- "p28_330_HET_009"

input_dir <- file.path(
  project_root,
  "data",
  sample_name,
  "raw"
)

input_file <- "p28_330_HET_009.tif"

output_dir <- file.path(
  project_root,
  "results",
  sample_name,
  "01_mgtoolbox_signal"
)

qc_dir <- file.path(output_dir, "figures")

dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(qc_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

input_path <- file.path(input_dir, input_file)

if (!file.exists(input_path)) {
  stop("Input TIFF was not found: ", project_relative(input_path))
}

# These values reproduce the settings of the existing p28 MGtoolbox object.
bio_dimensions <- c(210.42, 210.42, 48)
prior_soma_diameter <- 12
minimum_soma_volume <- 300
territory_mu <- 60
territory_sigma <- 3

cat("Project root: repository root\n")
cat("Input:", project_relative(input_path), "\n")
cat("Output directory:", project_relative(output_dir), "\n")
```

## 3. Read the 3D TIFF stack

```{r read-stack}
stack_list <- read_z_stacks(
  dir = input_dir,
  filename = input_file
)

image_stack <- stack_list[[input_file]]

dim(image_stack)
```

## 4. Construct the MGtoolbox stack object

```{r construct-stack-object}
so <- stackObj(
  image_stack,
  bio_dim = bio_dimensions,
  output_path = output_dir,
  stack_alias = sample_name
)

create_stackDir(so)

cat("stackObj dimensions:\n")
print(dim(stack(so)))

cat("Biological dimensions:\n")
print(bio_dim(so))

# visualize 

plot(so)
```

## 5. Detect somas

The MDR calculation is expensive. On the first run, the code creates and
saves it. On a later run, the existing MDR file is imported automatically.

```{r detect-somas}
mdr_file <- file.path(
  output_dir,
  sample_name,
  "MDR",
  paste0(sample_name, "_MDR.RDS")
)

use_existing_mdr <- file.exists(mdr_file)

cat("Use existing MDR:", use_existing_mdr, "\n")

so <- detect_somas(
  stackObj = so,
  prior_soma_diameter = prior_soma_diameter,
  min_soma_volume = minimum_soma_volume,
  import_MDR = use_existing_mdr,
  export_MDR = TRUE
)

soma_centroid_table <- as.data.frame(soma_centroids(so))
soma_cluster_table <- as.data.frame(soma_clusters(so))

cat("Number of detected somas:", nrow(soma_centroid_table), "\n")
print(soma_centroid_table)
```

## 6. Generate the MGtoolbox 3D detected-signal stack

```{r detected-territory}
signal_stack(so) <- stack(so)

so <- detected_territory(
  so,
  mu = territory_mu,
  sigma = territory_sigma
)

probability_3d <- so@detected_signal_stack

cat("3D MG probability dimensions (X, Y, Z):\n")
print(dim(probability_3d))

cat("3D MG probability summary:\n")
print(summary(as.vector(probability_3d)))

if (!identical(dim(probability_3d), dim(image_stack))) {
  stop("The 3D probability stack does not match the raw stack dimensions.")
}
```

## 7. Save the 3D results

```{r save-results}
stack_object_file <- file.path(
  output_dir,
  paste0(sample_name, "_stackObj_after_detected_territory.rds")
)

probability_3d_file <- file.path(
  output_dir,
  paste0(sample_name, "_mg_probability_3d.rds")
)

soma_centroid_file <- file.path(
  output_dir,
  paste0(sample_name, "_soma_centroids.csv")
)

soma_cluster_file <- file.path(
  output_dir,
  paste0(sample_name, "_soma_clusters.csv")
)

saveRDS(so, stack_object_file)
saveRDS(probability_3d, probability_3d_file)
write.csv(soma_centroid_table, soma_centroid_file, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(soma_cluster_table, soma_cluster_file, row.names = FALSE)

cat("Saved stackObj:\n", project_relative(stack_object_file), "\n")
cat("Saved 3D MG probability:\n", project_relative(probability_3d_file), "\n")
```

## 8. Save a QC maximum-intensity projection

This projection is only a visual quality-control image. The downstream 3D
analysis will use `probability_3d`, not this projection.

```{r save-qc}
probability_mip <- MIProject_im(probability_3d, along = 3)

qc_file <- file.path(
  qc_dir,
  paste0(sample_name, "_mg_probability_3d_mip_qc.png")
)

png(qc_file, width = 1600, height = 1600, res = 200)
par(mar = c(0, 0, 3, 0))
image(
  t(probability_mip)[, nrow(probability_mip):1],
  col = gray.colors(256),
  axes = FALSE,
  main = paste(sample_name, "MGtoolbox 3D probability MIP")
)
dev.off()

cat("Saved QC image:\n", project_relative(qc_file), "\n")
```

## 9. Save the run summary

```{r save-summary}
summary_file <- file.path(
  output_dir,
  paste0(sample_name, "_mg_probability_3d_summary.txt")
)

summary_lines <- c(
  paste0("sample=", sample_name),
  paste0("input=", project_relative(input_path)),
  paste0("input_dimensions_xyz=", paste(dim(image_stack), collapse = ",")),
  paste0("bio_dimensions=", paste(bio_dimensions, collapse = ",")),
  paste0("prior_soma_diameter=", prior_soma_diameter),
  paste0("minimum_soma_volume=", minimum_soma_volume),
  paste0("territory_mu=", territory_mu),
  paste0("territory_sigma=", territory_sigma),
  paste0("detected_somas=", nrow(soma_centroid_table)),
  paste0("probability_dimensions_xyz=", paste(dim(probability_3d), collapse = ",")),
  paste0("probability_min=", min(probability_3d, na.rm = TRUE)),
  paste0("probability_median=", median(probability_3d, na.rm = TRUE)),
  paste0("probability_mean=", mean(probability_3d, na.rm = TRUE)),
  paste0("probability_max=", max(probability_3d, na.rm = TRUE)),
  paste0("probability_3d_file=", project_relative(probability_3d_file)),
  paste0("stack_object_file=", project_relative(stack_object_file)),
  paste0("qc_file=", project_relative(qc_file))
)

writeLines(summary_lines, summary_file)

cat(paste(summary_lines, collapse = "\n"))
cat("\n\nMGtoolbox 3D generation completed successfully.\n")
```
